justification: New user-facing section in the paid conveyancing PDF backed by a new production-DB spatial query. Wrong wording carries misleading-conduct exposure (extent claims about a named property) and a silent DB failure could render as a false 'outside the mapped extent'. Not critical: read-only disclosure layer, no schema change, no write path, feature-flagged, and it does not feed the constraints tile or any verdict.

pre_impl.existing_data: spatial_overlays rows with layer_type='coastal_inundation' — 1,415 polygons loaded 2026-07-09 by scripts/ingest_coastal_inundation.py (committed in this PR), instrument_key estuary_inund_2025_s370_y{2050|2100}_{f1..f4}, value_numeric = days/year, currency_date 2025-11-24. Checked live in this session: per-key counts sum to 1,415 and a cadastre-resolved lot (propid 6021043) intersects f4 for both years.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If instrument_key drifts from the loader's pattern or value_numeric is NULL, the row is skipped; if ALL intersecting rows are unparseable the fetcher returns failed (renders 'not assessed'), never a fabricated year or a false 'outside'. If the layer is ever deleted, every lot reads 'outside' — that is the one honest-but-wrong state; mitigated by the loader + count being committed alongside the renderer in this PR.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Render-only change: applies to every PDF generated after deploy (service path fetches live per request; coastal is fetched in the PDF-exclusive stage, not stored in conveyancing_cache, so stale caches simply render without the section via the None default).

functions.name: get_coastal_inundation_live
functions.input: lat/lng floats + optional lot_wkt string from resolve_address; DATABASE_URL env
functions.output: three-state dict: failed | outside(query_basis) | intersects(query_basis, years{year: {days_per_year, value}})
functions.if_none: missing DATABASE_URL or any DB error returns {'status': 'failed'} — renders 'not assessed', never an extent claim; missing lot_wkt falls back to the point query and tags query_basis='point' for the caveat

functions.name: build_coastal_inundation_lines
functions.input: the fetcher dict (or None from stale callers) + report_date string
functions.output: render-state dict {render, state, rows, framing, scope_line, source_line, status_line, basis_note} consumed by generate_pdf
functions.if_none: None or unrecognised status returns render=False (section omitted — never a false claim); intersects with zero renderable years fails closed to the 'not assessed' line

functions.name: _coastal_year_row
functions.input: year int + per-year tier dict {days_per_year, value} read from the DB row
functions.output: one factual sentence per year, or None
functions.if_none: missing days_per_year returns None (row dropped) — a figure is never composed; unparseable pct in value omits the parenthetical rather than inventing one

functions.name: _fetch_coastal
functions.input: req.lat/req.lng + lot_wkt from the cached or re-run pipeline
functions.output: the fetcher dict passed to generate_pdf(coastal=...)
functions.if_none: any import/runtime exception returns {'status': 'failed'} so a broken deploy renders 'not assessed', not a crash or a false outside

values.if_missing: row skipped; if no row for a year survives, that year is absent from the section; if none survive at all the fetcher fails closed to 'not assessed'

values.value: years dict keys after any JSON boundary
values.if_missing: string keys from a JSON round-trip are int()-converted per row; tested in test_string_year_keys_tolerated

queries.purpose: lot-polygon (preferred) or point intersection against the estuarine inundation layer
queries.where_clause: WHERE layer_type = 'coastal_inundation' AND ST_Intersects(geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_GeomFromText(%s), 4326)) — point variant uses ST_Point(lng, lat); layer_type scope is the correctness filter (statewide layer; spatial_overlays has no LGA/is_active column to filter on)
queries.if_zero: status='outside' — an honest checked non-intersection (97% of NSW lots)
queries.if_wrong: worst case is an extent claim for the wrong lot; guarded upstream by GATE-0 parcel resolution supplying lot_wkt, and the point-basis caveat names the weaker basis when the polygon was unavailable

break_it.scenario: DB down at generation time renders as 'outside the mapped extent' on a canal-estate lot — a false clear in a legal document.
break_it.what_happens: Buyer reads an outside-extent claim that was never checked.
break_it.how: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2046 — no DATABASE_URL and every exception path return status='failed', which build_coastal_inundation_lines renders as the 'not assessed' line with no extent claim; 'outside' is only reachable after a query that ran and returned zero rows. Tests: test_no_database_url_fails_not_outside, test_connect_error_fails_not_outside, test_failed_renders_not_assessed_without_extent_claim.
break_it.repro: unset DATABASE_URL and call get_coastal_inundation_live(-33.5, 151.3) — returns failed; section renders 'not assessed'

break_it.scenario: A malformed instrument_key or NULL value_numeric row poisons the year selection, inventing a year or frequency.
break_it.what_happens: A fabricated figure appears in a conveyancer-facing disclosure.
break_it.how: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2083 — unparseable rows are skipped and never invent a year; all-unparseable falls to status='failed' (a data defect must not read as checked-outside). Figures are READ from the stored value/value_numeric, never composed. Tests: test_malformed_rows_skipped_all_malformed_fails_closed, test_malformed_row_does_not_poison_valid_year, test_year_figures_read_from_rows_never_composed.

break_it.scenario: The section reads as general 'coastal' coverage, so a beachfront (open-surf, non-estuary) buyer treats 'outside the mapped extent' as an all-clear for coastal inundation.
break_it.what_happens: Inclusion/omission trap — the report implies coverage the dataset does not have.
break_it.how: The scope sentence (estuarine only; does NOT cover open-coast/surf inundation or erosion, nor riverine flooding) rides with EVERY rendered extent claim — outside and intersects states both; the anchor term everywhere is 'estuarine tidal inundation'. Tests: test_every_extent_claim_scoped_estuarine, test_outside_carries_scope_and_source.
break_it.repro: read either generated PDF: scope sentence present under the section in both the intersects (Louth Park) and outside (Bowral) states

break_it.scenario: Point-based fallback (no lot polygon) misses an extent that clips only the lot edge, and the report presents the point check as a lot check.
break_it.what_happens: Partial-lot intersections read as outside with no signal of the weaker basis.
break_it.how: query_basis is threaded from the fetcher and the point basis renders an explicit caveat naming that the lot polygon was unavailable and a lot-boundary check can differ. Test: test_point_basis_gets_caveat_note.
break_it.repro: call get_coastal_inundation_live without lot_wkt — result carries query_basis='point'; builder emits the basis note
